grade.first_issue: Newton’s inequality \(S_j^2>S_{j-1}S_{j+1}\) does not imply that \(S_{j-1}\) and \(S_{j+1}\) have the same sign.
grade.summary: The contradiction setup and nonvanishing argument are correct, but the central passage to strict log-concavity of \((|S_j|)\) is invalid. If \(S_{j-1}S_{j+1}<0\), Newton’s inequality is automatic and gives no corresponding absolute-value inequality. Consequently, the decreasing-ratio estimate and factorial bound on \(|c_k|\) are unsupported.
strengths: Correctly observes that the assumed \(k\) distinct roots force \(c_k\ne0\), allowing integrality to yield \(|c_k|\ge1\).
The recursive contradiction would be valid if the asserted absolute log-concavity estimate had been established.

errors.description: The false sign inference invalidates \(|S_j|^2>|S_{j-1}||S_{j+1}|\), on which the entire coefficient bound and final contradiction depend.
